slides.title: Meet Bolt
slides.text: Bolt is a robot. Bolt does exactly what you tell it, one step at a time. It never guesses what you meant.
slides.alt: Bolt the robot at the start of a short dotted path, with the goal flag four squares ahead and an empty program tray.

focus.cue: This is Bolt. It only does what you tell it.
The flag is four squares away.

slides.title: Steps in order
slides.text: A list of steps in order is called an algorithm. When you join blocks together for Bolt, you write a program: the algorithm in blocks.
slides.alt: Bolt's program tray holds four move blocks stacked in order, matching the four dotted squares between Bolt and the flag.

focus.cue: Four move blocks, joined in order: that is the program.
The blocks run first to last, walking Bolt to the flag.

slides.title: Turn first, then move
slides.text: Bolt faces along the top row, but the flag waits at the bottom of the board. First Bolt turns right to aim down the left side, then it moves.
slides.alt: Bolt at the top left, facing along the top row, the flag at the bottom right, and a tray that starts turn right, move, move.

focus.cue: First: turn right. The turn aims Bolt before any step.
The flag waits below: every block has to aim Bolt right.

slides.title: A turn does not move
slides.text: A turn block spins Bolt in place to face a new way. Only a move block takes Bolt to the next square.
slides.alt: Bolt has driven four squares, then turned left in the same square to face the flag; the turn block is lit in the tray.

focus.cue: Bolt turned in this same square: it did not move.
The turn block, lit up, is the one that just ran.
Only the move blocks carried Bolt along this trail.

slides.title: Pick the better route
slides.text: Two routes can both reach the flag. The better one is shorter, safer or easier to get right. A long dry route beats a short wet one! Split a long route into legs.
slides.alt: The compare screen before a route is picked: Route A takes 7 blocks, Route B takes 8, and a green Use button sits under each one.

focus.cue: Route B: 8 blocks. One more chance to go wrong.
Tap Use under a route to load it into the tray.

words.means: a list of steps in order
the order the steps go in
one thing to do, like one block
an algorithm written for a computer, like your blocks

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Sequences and finish all 6 levels. Before you press Run, point at each block and say what Bolt will do.
slides.alt: Bolt the robot at the start of a short dotted path, with the goal flag four squares ahead and an empty program tray.

focus.cue: Your turn: build a program, then point at each block.
